title: SRE SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, and Runbook Standards
author: Ari Chen
content:
Summary

This document defines Redwood Inference's standard approach for SRE documentation covering SLOs and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, operational tooling, and runbooks. The goal is to provide a single, consistent reference for service owners, on-call engineers, and platform teams to define, measure, and act on reliability goals.

Table of contents
1. Purpose and scope
2. SLOs and error budgets (definitions & examples)
3. Capacity planning and scaling policy
4. Operational tooling and dashboards
5. Runbook standards and on-call playbooks
6. Incident review and postmortem standards
7. Reliability initiatives and prioritization
8. Ownership, cadence, and audit checklist
9. Appendix: templates and examples

1. Purpose and scope
This doc applies to all services that directly impact customer-facing inference (hosted API, dedicated inference pools, private control plane) and their supporting infra (routing, cache, auth, telemetry). It standardizes how we:
- Define measurable SLOs and derive error budgets
- Plan capacity and scaling for predictable throughput and latency
- Author and maintain operational runbooks and escalation steps
- Conduct consistent incident reviews and follow-up reliability initiatives

2. SLOs and error budgets
Principles
- SLOs are customer-facing and measure end-to-end user experience (latency & correctness for generation/chat requests, embedding throughput, control-plane availability).
- Every production service must have at least one SLO and an associated error budget tracked in the centralized SLO dashboard.
- SLOs are expressed as a percentage over a rolling window (commonly 7d and 30d). Error budgets are consumed by incidents and steady-state failures.

Standard SLO types and examples
| Service | SLO metric | Window | Target | Measurement details | Owner |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| Redwood API (text-generation) | P95 tail latency (server-side) for synchronous generation (<= 2s) | 30d | 99.0% | Synthetic + production tracing; exclude known maintenance windows | inference-api-team |
| Redwood API (streaming) | Time-to-first-byte (TTFB) | 30d | 99.5% | Measured from request arrival to first stream chunk | inference-api-team |
| Embeddings endpoint | 99th percentile latency | 7d | 99.0% | Batch and single-shot measured separately | embeddings-team |
| Control plane | API availability (5xx rate) | 30d | 99.95% | Aggregated by endpoint, excludes scheduled deploys | control-plane |

Error budget policy and burn rates
- Error budget = (1 - SLO_target) * window.
- Burn rate thresholds:
  - Normal: burn_rate <= 1 -> Continue normal operations.
  - Elevated: 1 < burn_rate <= 3 -> Immediate mitigation steps; owners notified.
  - Critical: burn_rate > 3 -> Stop launches, trigger reliability war room, create urgent action items.
- Burn rate is calculated as: (observed_errors / expected_allowed_errors) over a short window (typically 1h or 6h) depending on SLO criticality.

Enforcement and governance
- If burn rate enters Elevated, the on-call overseer must:
  1) Notify product and engineering leads.
  2) Evaluate rollback or capacity actions.
  3) Create a short-term mitigation plan in the incident tracker.
- If Critical: an incident is declared and the incident review process must be initiated within 24 hours of mitigation start.

3. Capacity planning and scaling policy
Capacity planning objectives
- Ensure headroom for 99th-percentile expected traffic spikes and for service degradation fallbacks (e.g., model variant fallback).
- Keep reserve buffer to satisfy latency SLOs during autoscaling cold-starts and rolling upgrades.

Inputs and data sources
- Traffic forecasts: 90/95/99th percentile weekly and monthly forecasts (from traffic-calc pipeline).
- Performance profiles: throughput-per-GPU, memory footprint, KV cache hit ratios (from benchmarking registry).
- Historical incident & throttle logs (capacity reductions in prior incidents).

Planning cadence and artifacts
- Quarterly capacity review per product area with owners, infra, and SRE. Deliverables: capacity plan document, scale/test schedule, and risk matrix.
- Monthly telemetry sanity checks to validate forecast accuracy.

Scaling policies and guardrails
- Autoscaling targets: keep average GPU utilization < 70% for production pools; burst headroom must accommodate 5 minute 99th-percentile traffic without SLO violation.
- Pre-warm policy: for scheduled heavy events, request pre-warmed capacity 24-48 hours before the event.
- Cost vs latency tradeoff: use conservative quantization and batching profiles recommended by Redwood Optimize when throughput demands increase.

Capacity test playbook (high level)
1) Define test goal: e.g., confirm P95 latency < SLO at 2x predicted peak.
2) Select canary cluster with mirror traffic and synthetic load generator.
3) Ramp traffic incrementally while monitoring SLOs, error budget burn, and GPU metrics.
4) Stop at first SLO breach, record root cause, and remediate.

4. Operational tooling and dashboards
Required tooling (minimum stack)
- Metrics: Prometheus for service metrics; pushgateway for short-lived jobs.
- Long-term storage and queries: Cortex/Thanos or hosted TSDB; central queries for SLO dashboards.
- Tracing: Jaeger/Tempo for distributed traces; sample retention policy documented.
- Logs: Loki/ELK for structured logs with correlation IDs.
- Alerts and incident management: PagerDuty for paging, Opsgenie or Jira for followup tasks.
- Dashboards: Grafana with templated SLO and runbook links.

Standard dashboards and alerts
- SLO dashboard: 30d & 7d windows, highlight remaining error budget and burn rate.
- On-call runbook panel: quick links to runbooks for top 10 pages.
- Capacity dashboard: GPU utilization, queue depths, KV cache hit rates, model inference latencies.
- Alerting thresholds: alerts map to severity (P1/P2/P3) and include runbook link, recent deploys, and owner.

Data retention and access
- Metrics: 13 months for aggregated SLO data; 90 days for high-resolution (1s/10s) metrics.
- Traces: 90 day retention for sampled traces; retain full traces for major incidents indefinitely in cold storage.
- Access control: dashboards and query editors are RBAC-protected; editing requires reviewer approval.

5. Runbook standards and on-call playbooks
Runbook requirements (every production runbook must include)
- Runbook title and service tag
- Owner and secondary contact (team slack, pager duty escalation chain)
- Preconditions (SLO breached, specific alert fired)
- Immediate actions (first 10 minutes): checklist of steps to stabilize
- Diagnostic commands and queries with examples (PromQL, curl, kubectl, model-serving CLI)
- Mitigation steps and safe rollbacks
- Post-stabilization tasks and links to incident template
- Last-reviewed date and reviewer names

Example immediate actions (API high-5xx rate)
1) Confirm incident via SLO dashboard and logs.
2) Identify recent deploys (last 30m) and roll back if release correlates with error spike.
3) If spike is capacity-related, increase pool capacity (uses reserved burst or scale-up) and apply temporary rate-limiting via gateway.
4) Notify product and security if customer data may be impacted.

Standard command snippets (examples)
- PromQL to check P95 latency: 100 * (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le)))
- Check pod restarts: kubectl get pods -l app=inference-api -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount}'
- Temporarily reduce concurrency on gateway: curl -X POST https://gateway.internal/api/v1/config -d '{"max_concurrency": 50}'

6. Incident review and postmortem standards
Postmortem template (required for incidents that consume > 10% of an SLO error budget or are P1)
- Title and incident ID
- Summary (one-paragraph): what happened and customer impact
- Timeline: ordered events with timestamps (UTC)
- Root cause analysis: one-sentence root cause and supporting evidence
- Mitigations taken: immediate and short-term actions
- Long-term action items: owner, target date, verification plan
- Lessons learned and preventive measures
- Error budget impact and metrics
- Postmortem reviewer signoff

Blamelessness and tone
- Reviews are blameless: focus on why the system allowed the failure and how to prevent recurrence.
- Action items should be small, specific, and timeboxed (owner + due date).

7. Reliability initiatives and prioritization
Initiative intake and scoring
- Initiatives are proposed through the reliability backlog (Jira project REL-100). Each initiative must include: business impact, SLO improvement estimate, engineering effort estimate, and verification plan.
- Scoring rubric (example):
  - Customer impact (0-5), SLO delta (0-5), Implementation effort (0-5 inverted), Risk reduction (0-5) -> prioritize by weighted score.

Typical initiative types
- Observability improvements (SLO instrumentation, more robust sampling)
- Capacity & autoscaling improvements (pre-warm, faster scale-up paths)
- Runtime optimizations (kernel selection, batching improvements)
- Guardrails and automated remediation (auto-scale beyond threshold; automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant)

Verification and measurement
- Each completed initiative must have a verification playbook: how we measure SLO improvement and the date range for evaluation (typically 30-90 days post-deploy).

8. Ownership, cadence, and audit checklist
Roles and responsibilities
- Service Owner: defines SLOs and owns runbook correctness.
- SRE/On-call Engineer: maintains tooling, alerts, and executes runbooks for incidents.
- Platform Team: provides capacity and scaling primitives and enforces quotas.
- Product/PM: prioritizes reliability initiatives and approves SLO changes that affect customers.

Cadence and meetings
- Weekly on-call sync: 30 minutes to review active error budget burn and escalations.
- Monthly SLO review: owners review SLOs, thresholds, and recent burn behavior.
- Quarterly capacity planning review: cross-team planning with infra and product.

Audit checklist (minimum for SRE audit)
- [ ] Service SLO defined in SLO dashboard
- [ ] Runbook exists and was reviewed in last 90 days
- [ ] Alerts map to runbook and have owners assigned
- [ ] Capacity plan updated in last quarter
- [ ] Incident postmortems posted for P1s or >10% error budget incidents
